description: Geometric convexity of the continuous-time American put option exercise boundary in the constant-parameter Black-Scholes model; issue #175.

theorems.name: American Put Option Logarithmic Exercise Boundary Convexity
theorems.description: For positive strike K, risk-free interest rate r and volatility sigma, and constant dividend yield 0 <= q <= r, the logarithm log(B(tau)/K) of the continuous-time American put option exercise boundary is convex in positive time-to-expiry tau. B is defined from the optimal-stopping value on the completed usual filtration of the constructed Brownian motion. The conclusion is geometric convexity, not strict logarithmic curvature or existence of classical second derivatives. The literature recorded convexity as open for 0 < q < r (proved at q = 0, disproved for q > r); this entry covers that whole region, resolving the open problem.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanPut.Stopping.PhysicalBoundaryConvexity

open Set
open MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanPut.Stopping

theorem american_put_log_boundary_convex {K r q σ : ℝ}
    (hK : 0 < K) (hr : 0 < r) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hqr : q ≤ r) (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0)
      (fun τ : ℝ => Real.log (brownianUsualExerciseBoundary K r q σ τ.toNNReal / K)) :=
  MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanPut.Stopping.brownianUsualLogBoundary_convexOn hK hr hq hqr hσ

metadata.reference: Robert Martin, Log-convexity of the exercise boundary of an American put option; source development https://github.com/robertmartin8/AmericanPutConvexity/tree/9b2b208520341a63b64eef43c1ecb3c5708a8e63; MathFin issue #175.
metadata.formalization_scope: Derived from the concrete stopping-value definition, not from an assumed classical free-boundary solution or a convexity specification. Admissible rules are all stopping times of the constructed completed usual Brownian filtration with values pointwise bounded by the horizon; AEHorizonValue proves equality with the value and threshold obtained from extended stopping times bounded by the horizon only almost surely. The value uses GBM with drift r-q and discount rate r. The proof derives the normalized boundary and its line-interval property using a straight-line comparison, a parabolic three-point argument and a terminal barrier, then proves geometric convexity and rescales to physical units. Covers q=0 and q=r as well as 0<q<r, only at positive time-to-expiry. Does not assert universality over arbitrary probability-space representations, C2 regularity, strict log-convexity, or a result for q>r.

theorems.name: American Put Option Exercise Boundary Strict Convexity
theorems.description: For positive strike K, risk-free interest rate r and volatility sigma, and constant dividend yield 0 <= q <= r, the continuous-time American put option exercise boundary B(tau) is strictly convex in positive time-to-expiry tau. B is defined from the optimal-stopping value on the completed usual filtration of the constructed Brownian motion. Strict convexity is in the chord-inequality sense; the statement does not assert a classical second derivative or B'' > 0. The literature recorded convexity as open for 0 < q < r (proved at q = 0, disproved for q > r); this entry covers that whole region, resolving the open problem.

metadata.formalization_scope: Derived for the same actual stopping boundary as the logarithmic-convexity entry. The proof first obtains nonstrict convexity of the logarithmic boundary using only its nonincrease. A terminal barrier excludes a flat tail, so convexity and nonincrease imply strict decrease; strict convexity of the exponential then yields strict convexity of the stock-price boundary. The physical-unit theorem assumes only K>0, r>0, sigma>0 and 0<=q<=r. Its domain is positive time-to-expiry. No boundary-smoothness premise is imposed, and no classical second-derivative or q>r conclusion is claimed.

theorems.name: American Put Exercise Boundary Tends to the Strike at Expiry
theorems.description: For positive strike K, risk-free rate r, dividend yield q with 0 <= q <= r, and volatility sigma, the continuous-time American put exercise boundary B(tau) tends to the strike K as time-to-expiry tau decreases to 0. B is defined from the optimal-stopping value on the completed usual filtration of the constructed Brownian motion, the same boundary as the convexity entries above. Only the parameter cell 0 < r, 0 <= q <= r is covered; q > r > 0, q < 0 and negative rates are not treated, since the underlying boundary theory assumes this cell.

theorems.name: QD+ Fixed-Point Integrand Endpoint Limit (Differentiable Boundary)
theorems.description: The Andersen-Lake-Offengenden fixed-point scheme for the American put exercise boundary integrates, at collocation node tau with trial boundary value b, an explicit integrand K12 built from an interpolated boundary B via the Black-Scholes d+ term, after the substitution m = tau*(1+y)^2/4 used by a Gauss-Lobatto quadrature rule on y in [-1,1]. At the endpoint y = -1 (m = 0) the time argument of d+ vanishes, giving a 0/0 form on the diagonal b = B(tau); this is the one-sided limit that resolves it. When B is differentiable at tau with B(tau) > 0 and b = B(tau), K12(y) tends to exp(q*tau)*(sqrt(tau)/sigma)/sqrt(2*pi) as y -> -1 from above. This is transcribed from QuantLib's qdfpamericanengine.cpp over an abstract boundary B, with no fixed-point or pricing content.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanQDPlusLimits

open Filter MathFin
open scoped Topology Real

theorem qdplus_k12_endpoint_differentiable_thm {B : ℝ → ℝ} {r q σ τ : ℝ}
    (hσ : 0 < σ) (hτ : 0 < τ) (hB : DifferentiableAt ℝ B τ) (hBpos : 0 < B τ) :
    Tendsto (qdfpK12 B r q σ τ (B τ)) (𝓝[>] (-1))
      (𝓝 (Real.exp (q * τ) * (Real.sqrt τ / σ) / Real.sqrt (2 * π))) :=
  tendsto_qdfpK12_endpoint hσ hτ hB hBpos

The sibling integrands K3, ni, di have matching endpoint-limit theorems in the same file (tendsto_qdfpK3_endpoint, tendsto_qdfpNi_endpoint, tendsto_qdfpDi_endpoint), and each has an off-diagonal (b != B(tau)) counterpart tending to 0 or a step function instead. Axioms-clean. LIMITS: purely the one-sided limit of the printed quadrature integrand; no claim about the fixed-point iteration's convergence, the boundary B itself, or American-option pricing accuracy.

theorems.name: QD+ Endpoint Limit: Differentiability Cannot Be Weakened to Continuity
theorems.description: The QD+ fixed-point integrand K12's endpoint limit at y = -1 on the diagonal b = B(tau) (exp(q*tau)*(sqrt(tau)/sigma)/sqrt(2*pi), the value QuantLib's quadrature rule implicitly assumes) requires the boundary B to be differentiable at tau, not merely continuous. For the continuous, 1/2-Holder boundary B(s) = b*exp(-c*sqrt(tau-s)) (so B(tau) = b), the same integrand instead tends to exp(q*tau)*(sqrt(tau)/sigma)*phi(c/sigma), which differs from the differentiable-case value whenever c != 0. This pair (the Holder boundary's own limit, and its distinctness from the differentiable-case value) shows the differentiability hypothesis is not an artifact of the proof technique.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanQDPlusLimits

open Filter MathFin
open scoped Topology Real

theorem qdplus_k12_endpoint_differentiability_tight_thm {r q σ τ b c : ℝ}
    (hσ : 0 < σ) (hτ : 0 < τ) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    Tendsto (qdfpK12 (fun s ↦ b * Real.exp (-(c * Real.sqrt (τ - s)))) r q σ τ b) (𝓝[>] (-1))
        (𝓝 (Real.exp (q * τ) * (Real.sqrt τ / σ) * gaussianPDFReal 0 1 (c / σ))) ∧
      ¬ Tendsto (qdfpK12 (fun s ↦ b * Real.exp (-(c * Real.sqrt (τ - s)))) r q σ τ b) (𝓝[>] (-1))
        (𝓝 (Real.exp (q * τ) * (Real.sqrt τ / σ) / Real.sqrt (2 * π))) :=
  ⟨tendsto_qdfpK12_endpoint_holder hσ hτ hb,
    not_tendsto_qdfpK12_endpoint_holder hσ hτ hb hc⟩

metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof, MathFin/BlackScholes/AmericanQDPlusLimits.lean (tendsto_qdfpK12_endpoint_holder, not_tendsto_qdfpK12_endpoint_holder), bundled here as a conjunction of the two theorems for a single benchmark entry. The continuous boundary B(s) = b*exp(-c*sqrt(tau-s)) is an explicit counterexample, not a generic continuous boundary; the claim is only that continuity alone does not pin down the endpoint value QuantLib's quadrature assumes. Axioms-clean.
